message.content:
I don’t have real‑time access to live air‑quality feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
Here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to check |
|--------|--------------|
| **EPA AirNow** | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It shows the current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), and health advisories. |
| **AirVisual / IQAir** | Go to <https://www.iqair.com/usa/california/los-angeles> or <https://www.airvisual.com/city/us/los-angeles>. They provide a live map, hourly updates, and forecast. |
| **Weather Apps** | Many weather apps (e.g., Weather Underground, AccuWeather, The Weather Channel) include an AQI widget. |
| **Mobile Apps** | “AQICN” (Air Quality Index) and “Plume Labs: Air Report” give real‑time readings and alerts. |

If you’re looking for historical trends or a deeper analysis, the EPA’s AirNow API or the World Air Quality Index project offer programmatic access. Let me know if you’d like help setting up an automated check!
